title: Hark! upon the Morning Breezes
description: Hark! upon the Morning Breezes in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911), headed “Christmas”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! up-on the morn-ing breez-es, In the dark-ness, ere the wa-king, Mu-sic sweet the sens-es pleas-es, Soft up-on the still-ness break-ing; "Glo-ry, Glo-ry!" this the sing-ing, Wel-come to Im-ma-nuel bring-ing.

lines: In the darkness, ere the waking,
Light is breaking on our blindness.
God is with us, truth surprising;
List to song the message voicing, —
Full of pity for our weakness; —
God hath made with man His dwelling.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
